hooks.text: A human could fly under muscle power alone across Saturn's moon Titan.
Could a human flap artificial wings and fly across Saturn's moon Titan?
You could fly across Saturn's moon Titan using only your arms.

title: The Moon Where Humans Can Fly
description: Titan's dense atmosphere and weak gravity create a world where a human equipped with artificial wings could take off and fly under their own muscle power.

beats.text: A human could fly under muscle power alone across Saturn's moon Titan.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a human flying with wings on Titan

beats.text: Christiaan Huygens discovered this massive world in 1655, larger in diameter than the planet Mercury.
beats.visual: Historical painted portrait of Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens, 1671

beats.text: It is the only moon in our solar system with a dense atmosphere and stable surface liquids.
beats.visual: Cassini natural color view of Titan's orange atmosphere, 2012

beats.text: At minus 179 degrees Celsius, liquid methane falls as rain, carving river valleys into Kraken Mare.
beats.visual: Cassini radar mosaic of Kraken Mare and northern seas on Titan, 2014

beats.text: On January 14, 2005, the Huygens probe landed and photographed rounded pebbles of frozen water ice.
beats.visual: Huygens lander photograph of rounded water ice boulders on Titan, 2005

beats.text: Titan's surface atmospheric pressure is roughly 1.5 times that of Earth at sea level.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of the Huygens probe descending through orange haze, 2005

beats.text: Because its gravity is so weak, that dense air provides incredible aerodynamic lift.
beats.visual: Cassini view of the detached blue haze layer in Titan's upper atmosphere, 2004

beats.text: Strap simple artificial wings to your arms and you could flap directly into the sky.
beats.visual: Artist's illustration of human flight using artificial wings on Titan

beats.text: No other world makes it so easy to take flight.
beats.visual: Cassini natural color view of Saturn and its moon Titan, 2012

better_than_last: Applied ep110 and ep129 lessons by using an active mystery hook and an abrupt, non-summary loop to maximize engagement and rewatch potential.
